Put $A=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$, $q=v^2$, $N\ge1$, $r\ge0$, $V=A^N$, and $T=V^{\otimes r}$. Let $U_{\mathbb Q(v)}(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ have the presentation of [[def-hh-type-a-quantum-tensor-action-for-centralizers]] with its indeterminate renamed $v$ and its diagonal generators written $K_j$. Define $U_A$ to be its $A$-subalgebra generated by $K_j^{\pm1}$, $E_i^{(a)}=E_i^a/[a]_v!$, $F_i^{(a)}=F_i^a/[a]_v!$, and
$$\begin{bmatrix}K_j;0\\t\end{bmatrix}=\prod_{s=1}^t\frac{K_jv^{1-s}-K_j^{-1}v^{s-1}}{v^s-v^{-s}}\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Use $K_je_b=v^{\delta_{jb}}e_b$, $E_ie_b=\delta_{b,i+1}e_i$, $F_ie_b=\delta_{b,i}e_{i+1}$ and the coproduct
$$\Delta(E_i)=1\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes K_iK_{i+1}^{-1},\qquad\Delta(F_i)=K_i^{-1}K_{i+1}\otimes F_i+F_i\otimes1,\qquad\Delta(K_j)=K_j\otimes K_j.$$
The resulting action preserves $T$ and commutes with the right $H_{A,q}(S_r)$ action
$$e_{\ldots ab\ldots}T_s=\begin{cases}v e_{\ldots ba\ldots}&a<b,\\q e_{\ldots aa\ldots}&a=b,\\(q-1)e_{\ldots ab\ldots}+v e_{\ldots ba\ldots}&a>b.\end{cases}$$
It gives a surjection
$$\rho:U_A\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{H_{A,q}(S_r)}(T)\cong S_A(N,r)$$
onto the actual permutation-module endomorphism algebra of [[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]. Its composition-weight projections are
$$1_\mu=\rho\left(\prod_{j=1}^N\begin{bmatrix}K_j;0\\\mu_j\end{bmatrix}\right)\qquad(\mu\in\Lambda(N,r)).$$
Every statement survives any homomorphism $A\to R$ to a commutative ring, including parameters at arbitrary roots of unity; $S_A\otimes_A R$ is the actual specialized endomorphism algebra. The proof supplies a terminating exact divided-power expression for each integral orbit-basis map, with Laurent-unit pivots.

Let $\tau$ be the antiautomorphism $E_i\leftrightarrow F_i$, $K_j\mapsto K_j$, let $*$ be the current cellular antiautomorphism of $S_A$, and put $C=\sum_\mu c_\mu1_\mu$, $c_\mu=v^{-\sum_j\binom{\mu_j}{2}}$. Then
$$\rho(\tau(u))=C^{-1}\rho(u)^*C\qquad(u\in U_A).$$

There is also a square-root-free version over $B=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. On the permutation-module word basis define weight-block operators $\mathcal E_{i,a,\mu}$ and $\mathcal F_{i,a,\mu}$, zero outside content $\mu$, by replacing a subset $J$ of $a$ occurrences of $i+1$ by $i$, or of $i$ by $i+1$, respectively, with coefficients
$$q^{\sum_{j\in J}\#i(w_{>j})},\qquad q^{\sum_{j\in J}\#(i+1)(w_{<j})}.$$
Together with $1_\mu$ these generate $S_B(N,r)$. After $q=v^2$ they are precisely $v^{a(\mu_{i+1}-a)}\rho(E_i^{(a)})1_\mu$ and $v^{a(\mu_i-a)}\rho(F_i^{(a)})1_\mu$. Thus this generating assertion holds over every original coefficient ring with any unit $q$, whether or not $q$ has a square root. This assertion concerns the displayed polynomial action algebra; it does not assert a quantum group presentation over the original ring without choosing $v$.

Over every commutative $A$-algebra $R$, every cyclic polynomial left $U_R$-module of degree $r$, generated by a vector of weight $\lambda$ killed by every positive divided generator, is a quotient of $Q_R(\lambda)$. Equivalently, the left Weyl cell is the polynomial highest-induced module $S_R\otimes_{S_R^+}R_\lambda$, where $S_R^+$ is the image of the integral toral-positive subalgebra and $R_\lambda$ is its highest character. This statement includes the zero module and uses the actual composition-weight projections, rather than separation of specialized $K_j$ eigenvalues.

Fix $r\ge1$ and a skew shape $\nu/\lambda$ (for a partition shape take
$\lambda=\varnothing$), let $k\in\{1,\dots,r-1\}$, and let $T$ be a
semistandard skew tableau of shape $\nu/\lambda$ with entries in
$\{1,\dots,r\}$ ([[def-skew-diagram-and-semistandard-skew-tableau]],
[[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]). Call an entry $k$ or $k+1$ of
$T$ **free** if there is no $k+1$ respectively no $k$ in the same column. Then:

(i) the free positions in each row occupy consecutive cells of that row;
(ii) replacing in every row the free $k$'s and free $k+1$'s by their
complementary counts (if the row has $a_i$ free $k$'s and $b_i$ free $k+1$'s,
then after the replacement it has $b_i$ free $k$'s and $a_i$ free $k+1$'s in
the same free cells, the remaining entries unchanged, the free cells filled
from left to right by the $b_i$ copies of $k$ followed by the $a_i$ copies of
$k+1$) produces again a semistandard skew tableau $\sigma_k(T)$ of the same
shape, with entries in $\{1,\dots,r\}$;
(iii) $\sigma_k$ is an involution of the set of semistandard skew tableaux of
shape $\nu/\lambda$ with the same set of free positions, and
$\operatorname{wt}(\sigma_k(T))=s_k\operatorname{wt}(T)$, where $s_k$ is the
transposition of $k$ and $k+1$ acting on weights
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]], with weights read as vectors
in $\mathbb Z^r$).

Consequently, for every weight $\alpha\in\mathbb Z^r_{\ge0}$ the number of
semistandard skew tableaux of shape $\nu/\lambda$ and weight $\alpha$ equals
the number of weight $s_k\alpha$, and the generating function
$\sum_Tx^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}$, over semistandard skew tableaux of shape
$\nu/\lambda$ with entries in $\{1,\dots,r\}$, is symmetric in
$x_1,\dots,x_r$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Construct the corner over the original $R,q$. Put $M_0=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Lambda(N-1,d-1)}m_\alpha H_{d-1}$. Length-additive parabolic coset bases identify $M_1=\bigoplus_\alpha m_{(\alpha,1)}H_d$ with $M_0\otimes_{H_{d-1}}H_d$, by $m_\alpha h\otimes a\mapsto m_\alpha ha$. Hence $f\mapsto f\otimes1$, extended by zero on the other summands, embeds the lower Schur algebra with identity $p=\sum_{\alpha_N=1}1_\alpha$. It is injective because the unit parabolic coset supplies a direct summand. The lower regular composition induces the upper regular type $\omega_*=(1^{d-1},0^{N-d},1)$, so $e_{\rm lower}pV=e_*V$. On that summand the lower Hecke corner acts by left multiplication by exactly $h\in H_{d-1}$ on $H_d$, since $h\otimes a\mapsto ha$.

Use the root convention $F_{i,i+1}=F_i$ and $F_{i,j}=vF_{i+1,j}F_i-F_iF_{i+1,j}$. In the negative algebra, its last-simple-root-degree-one part is spanned by $xF_{i,N}$ with $x$ in the negative lower Levi. Here is a direct spanning proof, requiring no specialized PBW independence. Every divided-simple-generator word of this degree has exactly one $F_{N-1}$, exponent one; all other generators belong to the lower Levi. Move each factor to its right past the current root using $$F_{i,N}F_{i-1}^{(s)}=v^{-s}F_{i-1}^{(s)}F_{i,N}+v^{-1}F_{i-1}^{(s-1)}F_{i-1,N},\qquad F_{i,N}F_i^{(s)}=v^sF_i^{(s)}F_{i,N}.$$ Other lower simple divided generators commute with $F_{i,N}$. The first identity follows from $vF_{i,N}F_{i-1}=F_{i-1}F_{i,N}+F_{i-1,N}$ and $F_{i-1,N}F_{i-1}=vF_{i-1}F_{i-1,N}$: induction on ordinary powers gives coefficient $v^{-1}[s]$, canceled with $[s]!$ in the generic algebra, leaving the displayed integral identity. The second and remaining commutations follow by inserting the root recurrence into the rank-two Serre identity and then inducting on the interval length; the only noncommuting lower adjacent endpoint is $i-1$, already treated. Each move removes one right factor, so it terminates. Triangular spanning and the highest-vector relations now show $W^1=\sum_iU^-_{N-1}F_{i,N}z_\lambda$. If $\lambda_i=\lambda_{i+1}$, the weight $\lambda-\epsilon_i+\epsilon_{i+1}$ is absent: its sorted weight strictly dominates $\lambda$, contrary to the tableau support. Thus $F_i z_\lambda=0$ and the root recurrence gives $F_{i,N}z_\lambda=-F_iF_{i+1,N}z_\lambda$. Iteration removes all nonremovable rows. Rows beyond the height contribute zero by nonnegative weight support. Therefore the claimed removable-row generators span integrally.

Order these rows as $i_1>\cdots>i_t$, so $\mu_j=\lambda(i_j)$ decreases in dominance, and let $W_j$ be the negative lower-Levi span of the first $j$ generators, with $W_0=0$. Inductively suppose $W_{j-1}$ is invariant. In $W^1/W_{j-1}$ every weight lies below a remaining generator weight by step 2.1, and $\mu_j$ is their maximum. Every positive divided generator kills the image of $F_{i_j,N}z_\lambda$, since its target weight is strictly above $\mu_j$. Triangular spanning makes its negative span invariant. The actual universal highest property gives a surjection $W_{N-1}(\mu_j)\to W_j/W_{j-1}$. This proves invariance and these integral surjections at each stage, without dividing a quantum integer.

Exactly one entry $N$ in a semistandard $\lambda$-tableau lies at a removable corner, and deleting it gives a semistandard $\lambda(i)$-tableau on $1,\ldots,N-1$. Conversely appending $N$ at that corner preserves semistandardness. Consequently the actual free ranks satisfy $\operatorname{rank}W^1=\sum_j\operatorname{rank}W_{N-1}(\mu_j)$. Over $\mathbb Q(v)$ the surjections of step 3.1 and this dimension equality force equality of every quotient dimension. The kernel of each integral surjection lies in the free $A$-module $W_{N-1}(\mu_j)$ and has generic rank zero; injectivity into its fraction-field extension therefore makes that kernel zero. Each integral quotient is thus the actual free lower Weyl module. Its freeness makes the successive short exact sequences split as $A$-module sequences, so arbitrary base change preserves the filtration injections, quotients and surjections. Generic dimensions were used only to prove kernels of explicit integral surjections vanish, not to replace a specialized construction.

Over a field let $B^-$ denote the actual lower Borel image. A $B^-$-map $W^1\to F_\mu$ is determined by its values at the generators of step 2.1; their weights are distinct, so its dimension is at most one and is zero off $\mu_j$. At $\mu_j$, quotient by $W_{j-1}$. This quotient has no weight above $\mu_j$, its $\mu_j$-space is the one-dimensional generator line by step 4.1, and later generator weights lie strictly below it. Taking that generator's coefficient, and zero on every other weight, is a well-defined nonzero $B^-$-map, since a nonconstant negative operator cannot reach $\mu_j$. This proves dimension exactly one. The universal highest property gives $\operatorname{Hom}(W_{N-1}(\mu),X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{B^+}(F_\mu,X)$ for every polynomial $X$: maps are exactly primitive vectors of that weight. Taking contravariant duals identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}_{B^-}(X^\tau,F_\mu)$. With $X=(W^1)^\tau$ this proves the first Hom assertion. With $X=L^1$, self-duality and the injection $L^1\hookrightarrow(W^1)^\tau$ give the upper bound and label restriction. For a primitive vector $x$ of any composition weight, the functional $y\mapsto B(x,y)$ on $L^1$, pulled back to $W^1$, is nonzero by the nondegenerate homogeneous form and kills every nonconstant negative lower operator by contravariance. Thus it is a $B^-$-map to the character of that weight. The same generator bound excludes all other primitive weights, without presupposing their dominance. The form's toral weight orthogonality ensures first-level projection commutes with this duality.

Record the precise coefficient test needed by lowering arguments. If $L^1\to\nabla_{N-1}(\lambda(i))$ is nonzero, compose with $W^1\to L^1$ and with the highest-weight coefficient in $\nabla$. The resulting $B^-$-functional is nonzero, hence nonzero at $F_{i,N}z_\lambda$ by step 5.1. Every nonempty cut product $F_{i,b_1}F_{b_1,b_2}\cdots F_{b_s,N}z_\lambda$ has a nonconstant lower-Levi factor to the left and is killed by this functional. Multiplying factors by the unit toral normalization used for $\widehat F$ changes only their nonzero scalar factors on these fixed weight vectors. Thus the same zero/nonzero test applies to the normalized cut products. This argument needs neither an inherited tensor norm nor a claimed full-Hom surjection at singular parameters.

The summands of types $\omega_*=(1^{d-1},0^{N-d},1)$ and $\omega=(1^d,0^{N-d})$ are both the actual regular module $H_d$. Their identity isomorphisms give block matrix units $u,v$ in $S$ with $uv=e_*$ and $vu=e$. Multiplication by $u$ and $v$ consequently identifies $eV$ with $e_*V$, transporting every lower Hecke operator to its actual upper corner inclusion. This proves the natural restriction isomorphism, including $d=1$, whose lower algebra and corner are $R$. In the tensor realization of [F1], on words containing exactly one $N$ every lower divided generator leaves that position untouched and applies its subset-sum formula to the remaining ordered positions. These are exactly the induced operators of step 1.2 under the actual tensor/permutation intertwiner. Weight projections agree as well, so [F1]'s lower surjectivity proves equality of the full lower actions. The weight-unit diagonal conjugation of [F2] restricts to this subspace and intertwines the same actions after left/right conversion. This verifies the quantum/cellular comparison at every specialization by explicit generators.

derivations.claim: For a partition $\lambda$, list addable pluses and removable minuses of residue $i$ from top to bottom and cancel $-+$ pairs by a last-in-first-out minus stack. Deleting the first surviving minus and adding the last surviving plus are inverse selected moves. Indeed changing the selected corner changes its sign; every other altered boundary corner has residue $i+1$ or $i-1$, different from $i$ even at $e=2$. Immediately before a first surviving minus the minus stack is empty, and every suffix prefix has at least as many remaining minus pushes as plus pops. After flipping that minus to plus, these conditions say precisely that this plus survives and no later plus does. Reversing the flip proves the converse. This retains the positions of the selected signs, not just their counts.

Good deletion preserves restrictedness. For a removable row $r$, only its gap and the gap immediately above can change: the former decreases by one and the latter increases by one. The only possible violation is $r>1$ and $\lambda_{r-1}-\lambda_r=e-1$. Then the removable corners in rows $r-1,r$ have equal residues, and their minus signs are adjacent in that residue word: the addable corners between them have residues differing by one. If the lower minus survives, the upper one also survives, since stack pops remove the lower minus first. The lower one therefore cannot be the first surviving minus. Cogood addition preserves restrictedness by the dual adjacent-plus argument: if its row gap were $e-1$, the later same-residue addable corner would survive whenever the earlier one did, contradicting selection of the last surviving plus. Hence step 1.1 gives inverse partial operations on the restricted vertex set.

Every nonempty restricted partition has a good deletion. Let $h$ be its height. Its bottom removable node has residue $\lambda_h-h$, while the only boundary node below it is the addable $(h+1,1)$ of residue $-h$. The difference $\lambda_h$ lies strictly between zero and $e$, so these residues differ. There is consequently no later same-residue plus to cancel that bottom minus. At least one minus survives in that residue, and its first surviving minus is a good node. By step 2.1 its deletion stays restricted. Repeating decreases the number of boxes and ends at the empty diagram; reversing gives cogood additions by step 1.1. All selections may be made by the least residue and then the prescribed extremal sign, using finite sets.

Thus [F1] identifies the recursively chosen head with the same simple module $D(\lambda)$ for every allowed $i$. Let $p>0$ and let $\mu$ be a $p$-restricted partition, so that
$\mu_i-\mu_{i+1}<p$ for all $i\ge1$
([[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]],
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). A node $(r,c)$ of
the Young diagram $[\mu]$ is an **$i$-node** if its residue
$$\operatorname{res}(r,c):=c-r\bmod p$$
equals $i\in\mathbb Z/p$; the $i$-nodes of $\mu$ are its addable and removable
nodes of residue $i$
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]).

**The reduced $i$-signature.** Fix $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ and list the $i$-nodes
of $\mu$ as $A_1,\dots,A_n$ from top to bottom, that is, in increasing row
index and, for equal row index, in increasing column index. Form the word
$\sigma=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n)$ with $\sigma_m=+$ if $A_m$ is addable and
$\sigma_m=-$ if $A_m$ is removable. Whenever $r<s$, $\sigma_r=-$,
$\sigma_s=+$ and $\sigma_{r+1}=\dots=\sigma_{s-1}=0$, replace $\sigma_r$ and
$\sigma_s$ by $0$; repeat until no $-$ lies to the left of a $+$. The
resulting **reduced $i$-signature** has the form $+\cdots+- \cdots-$ with the
zeros deleted, and the nodes attached to its signs are:

- the **normal $i$-nodes** of $\mu$ are the removable nodes corresponding to
  the $-$ signs of the reduced signature;
- the **good $i$-node** is the topmost (first listed) of the normal $i$-nodes;
- the **conormal $i$-nodes** of $\mu$ are the addable nodes corresponding to
  the $+$ signs of the reduced signature;
- the **cogood $i$-node** is the bottommost (last listed) of the conormal
  $i$-nodes.

Write $\varepsilon_i(\mu)$ and $\varphi_i(\mu)$ for the numbers of normal and
of conormal $i$-nodes of $\mu$; the good $i$-node exists exactly when
$\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$, and the cogood $i$-node exactly when
$\varphi_i(\mu)>0$. At most one good and at most one cogood $i$-node occur,
for each residue.

**Well-definedness.** Each reduction step deletes two nonzero entries, so any
sequence of steps terminates after at most $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ steps, and in
the resulting word no $-$ lies to the left of a $+$: otherwise, take two
nonzero entries that are consecutive among the nonzero entries of the current
word and are ordered $-$, $+$; all entries strictly between them are $0$ by
the choice, so the pair would still be reducible. Hence, after deleting the zero entries, a terminal word is
$+^a-^b$ for some $a,b\ge0$; cancelled positions remain in their original
places and need not form a contiguous block. The terminal word does not depend on the
order in which reducible pairs are chosen: two reducible pairs cannot overlap
partially, because an endpoint of one pair lying strictly inside the other
would be a nonzero entry in a position that the other pair requires to be
$0$, and pairs sharing exactly one endpoint would similarly place a nonzero
entry strictly inside the other pair; so any two reducible pairs are either
disjoint (and the corresponding steps commute) or equal, there are no
critical pairs, and the rewriting relation is locally confluent. Uniqueness follows
by induction on the number of nonzero entries. A terminal word admits no
step. Otherwise, two distinct first steps commute and reach a common word
after one further step each. All these successor words have fewer nonzero
entries, so the induction hypothesis identifies their terminal words. Thus
any two reduction sequences have the same terminal word; in it the first surviving $-$ and the last surviving
$+$ are unique positions whenever they exist. Thus the reduced signature,
the sets of normal and conormal nodes, and the good and cogood nodes are well
defined. The empty partition has the unique addable node $(1,1)$, of residue $0$,
and no removable nodes. Its $0$-signature is $(+)$ and its other signatures
are empty. Thus $\varepsilon_i(\varnothing)=0$ for every $i$,
$\varphi_0(\varnothing)=1$, and $\varphi_i(\varnothing)=0$ for $i\ne0$.
It has no good node and its cogood $0$-node is $(1,1)$.

**Convention warning.** The residue $c-r$ used here is the negative of
Brundan's $\ell$-residue $r-c$, and a removable node of $\mu$ is normal here
exactly when its transposed node is normal in Brundan's sense for the
transpose partition $\mu'$; lists of addable and removable nodes, and the
signs of the residues, must never be silently mixed between the two
conventions
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]],
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and write $\mu=\lambda'$, $L=\ell(w_\lambda)$ and $N=\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))$. Let $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$ with its DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$, the cell module $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ with its Murphy form $G_{\lambda'}$, and the sign automorphism $\theta$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]], and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ be the $\theta$-twisted cell module of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]]. Then:

1. There is a base-change compatible isomorphism of right $H$-modules $$\Phi_\lambda\colon P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta,\qquad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda)=m_0,\quad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda h)=m_0\theta(h)\ \ (h\in H),$$ where $m_0$ is the class of $x_{\lambda'}$ in $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and the right side is computed with the ordinary action on $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and read in the twist; in particular $\Phi_\lambda(e_t)=m_0\theta(T_{d_{\lambda'}(t)})$ for $t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda')$. For a class $m\in C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and any lift $\widetilde m\in M(\lambda')$, the inverse is $\Phi_\lambda^{-1}(m)=q^{-N}x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}\theta(\widetilde m)$, independently of the chosen lift.

2. With $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$ the transported form of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]] and $u_\lambda(q):=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}\in A^\times$, $$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$ over every commutative $R$ with $q\in R^\times$. No unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar occurs: $u_\lambda$ is the explicit unit $q^{N-L}$ in the fixed normalizations of this page.

3. Consequently $\Phi_\lambda$ maps the radical of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ onto the radical of $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$, the induced map between the quotients is an isomorphism, with the corresponding cell-form quotients $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a field, when the quotients are nonzero they are the simple heads; when the forms are identically zero, the displayed quotients are zero and no assertion about the actual module heads is made. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all divisibility submodules and their reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and the twist, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. No choice principle is used.

Let $R$ be a commutative unital ring, $q\in R^\times$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, $M=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Lambda(d,n)}M^\alpha$ and $S=\operatorname{End}_H(M)$. For a symmetric polynomial $f$ over $R$, put $z_f=f(L_1,\ldots,L_n)$ for the additive Hecke Jucys–Murphy elements. Right multiplication $\rho_{z_f}:m\mapsto mz_f$ is a central element of $S$. On the right Weyl cell $W^\lambda$ it acts by

$$a_\lambda(f)=f\bigl([c(A)]_q:A\in[\lambda]\bigr),\qquad c(r,s)=s-r.$$

The identity holds over every $R$ and unit $q$, without division by a quantum integer or a Gram determinant. In particular, if $R=F$ is a field of finite quantum characteristic $e\ge2$ and $L^\mu$ is a constituent of $W^\lambda$, then $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same multiset of residues $c(A)\bmod e$. Neither partition is required to be restricted or to survive the Hecke corner. This proves a necessary content-separation condition, not an assertion that equal content is sufficient for common-block membership.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional algebra and $M$ a finite-dimensional left
$A$-module.

- Its **radical** is
  $$   \operatorname{rad}(M)=J(A)M,   $$
  equivalently the intersection of the maximal submodules, by
  [[thm-module-radical-is-jacobson-radical-times-the-module]].

- Its **socle** $\operatorname{Soc}(M)$ is the sum of all simple submodules, as
  in [[def-socle-of-a-module]].

- Its **head** or **top** is the quotient
  $$   \operatorname{hd}(M):=M/\operatorname{rad}(M),   $$
  formed using [[def-quotient-module]].

- Its **Loewy series** is the descending radical filtration
  $$   M\supseteq \operatorname{rad}(M)\supseteq \operatorname{rad}^2(M)\supseteq\cdots   $$
  together with the corresponding semisimple layers
  $\operatorname{rad}^i(M)/\operatorname{rad}^{i+1}(M)$.

The simple subquotients appearing in the Loewy layers are simple in the sense
of [[def-simple-module]].
